steps: Scientists can synthesize new elements in the laboratory by bombarding the nuclei of atoms with high-energy particles.
These nuclear reactions produce new elements, many of which are heavier than uranium.
items.finalAnswer: New elements are synthesized by bombarding atomic nuclei with high-energy particles.

steps: The statement is partly correct: the nucleus is at the centre of an atom, and electrons move around it, as planets move around the Sun.
However, the resemblance is not exact. The planets are held in their orbits by gravitational force, whereas electrons are attracted to the positively charged nucleus by electrostatic force.
items.finalAnswer: An atom resembles the solar system in its central nucleus and surrounding electrons, but the forces holding them differ.
